entries.title: You can steer the Illustrated picture
entries.body: Illustrated mode has a box asking "How should it come out?", where you can say in your own words, typed or dictated, up to 400 characters, what you want from the picture. Your note is passed to the AI that plans the painting, and a Paint again button sits beside an existing picture so you can try another direction. Pictures already painted stay as they are.

entries.title: High-powered AI can be switched on while adding
entries.body: The page for adding an article has a second tick box, High-powered AI, beside the one for generating the main modes. Before, you could only switch it on from the article's Metadata page once it had been added. It is off by default and is not remembered from one article to the next.

entries.title: Live conversation shows what it is doing
entries.body: Talking to the article out loud shows one status (Connecting, Listening, Thinking, Speaking) and a sound-level meter from the moment the microphone opens. What is said appears once, at the end of the chat. A failure gives the reason and a Try again button; the microphone settings sit under Advanced, and the dictation button there is gone.

entries.title: Structure is told not to summarise the abstract
entries.body: When Structure outlines a newly added article, it is told to treat the title block, the abstract and the reference list as parts that only identify the piece: a short plain label, no summary, no question. The abstract is already the author's own summary. Summary and the Tweets thread are told the same about the title block and the reference list, though not the abstract; outlines already built are unchanged.

entries.title: Feedback filters show how many reports each holds
entries.body: In the Feedback dialog's Earlier tab, the All, Shipped and Not shipped filters each show how many of your reports they hold, and screen readers read the number properly. When a list is cut short, it says how many it is showing out of how many there are.

entries.title: The where-you-are marker scrolls with less redrawing
entries.body: The marker on the strip showing where you are in the article moves in a way that asks the browser to redraw much less as you scroll, in our tests in a desktop browser. It sits exactly where it did before.

entries.title: Opened margin notes are no longer cut off
entries.body: Opening a note in the margin beside the article showed its answer but left its question, title or headline cut off with an ellipsis; it wraps onto as many lines as it needs. A passage you asked about in chat is also shown there in the article's own typeface, since those are the author's words.
